evidence: MMW19 Lemma 3.1 read verbatim (STOC19 PDF, offset 31500). Statement: for s(n) >= n and l(n) >= s(n)^2 (both time constructible), there is a uniform AC circuit family for MCSP^A[s(n)] of ~O(2^n * s(n)/l(n)) size and O(n/log l(n)) depth using Circuit-Min-Merge^A[s(n)] oracle gates, each taking only l(n) input bits. Construction: a d-ary tree with d = l(n)/(100 s(n) log s(n)); each gate merges d child circuit descriptions (size <= s(n)) on disjoint intervals; leaves are the constant-size descriptions D_0^x of the 2^n truth-table bits; depth log_d(2^n) = O(n/log l). Output is the AND of the first output bits of the root-layer gates, and search-MCSP is obtained by ANDing with the root description. CORRECTION to the earlier G0011 note: the gate fan-in is d = Theta(l/(s log s)), not poly(s); the 'poly(s) inputs' phrase in MMW19 Section 1.2 is informal. Scope: this is an UPPER-BOUND (circuit) construction; it gives no lower bound and no hardness information by itself. Locality observation (not a result): the state passed between gates is a size-s circuit description, not a residual-row count, so a count of distinct residual rows is not the quantity this construction uses. The earlier cm-788c40e311db4102 run is not evidence (see CORRECTION). P vs NP progress in R1455: none.

proved_step: Formalization of S-54f648a904 (inclusion-exclusion for #F). Let F = C_1 and ... and C_m be a CNF over x_1..x_n. For S subset of [m] put L(S) = union of C_i over i in S, and N(S) = #{a in {0,1}^n : every literal of L(S) is false under a}. Then #F = sum over S of (-1)^|S| N(S). Moreover N(S) = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if L(S) contains no complementary pair {x, not-x}, and N(S) = 0 otherwise, where V(S) is the set of variables occurring in L(S). Proof: with f_i(a) = 1 iff C_i is falsified by a, [a satisfies F] = product over i of (1 - f_i(a)). Expanding gives sum over S of (-1)^|S| times product over i in S of f_i(a), and that product is 1 exactly when all literals of L(S) are false under a. Summing over a gives the identity. A consistent L(S) forces the values of V(S) and leaves n - |V(S)| variables free; an inconsistent L(S) has no satisfying-falsifying assignment.
